chapter: Childhood in Tyler, Beaumont and Houston
title: The roomer pianist who let him sit in
summary: A talented pianist rooming in the same house let Gus beat on his drum along with him, until the man lost his mind.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: Right, I'd not be humming anything, just be playing by myself. And it happened, where we were staying there was a guy that lived in one of the rooms. We were rooming in those places.
And he was a piano player. And he would sit in the room there, this lady, Mrs. Gibson, she had a piano. And he would start playing. He could really play. But --
-- he lost his mind. He went nuts on account of that, one night. So they sent him away. Well we didn't know he was nuts.
Yeah. Pity, huh? Guy with talent.
And he could really play piano.
Well, when you heard him play piano, would you --
I would go and sit in and beat on my drums, and he liked it.
So you really were getting a little experience.
Yes, just from different ones like that.
